```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("../R/report_functions.R")
construct <- "rwa"
lo <- 1; hi <- 7
scores <- list(
  rwa                 = paste0("rwa_", 1:9, "_r"),
  rwa_aggression      = paste0("rwa_", 1:3, "_r"),
  rwa_submission      = paste0("rwa_", 4:6, "_r"),
  rwa_conventionalism = paste0("rwa_", 7:9, "_r"))
primary <- "rwa"
```

{{< include _construct_template.qmd >}}

## Construct-specific checks

The KSA-3 scale is designed with three facets (aggression, submission, conventionalism; three items each). The table compares a one-factor and a three-factor solution in every wave.

```{r rwa-efa}
fits <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(w) rbind(
  efa_loadings(d, scores$rwa, 1, w)$fit,
  efa_loadings(d, scores$rwa, 3, w)$fit)))
kable_out(fits)
```

**Wave 1 loadings, three factors** (loadings below .30 hidden):

```{r rwa-load}
kable_out(efa_loadings(d, scores$rwa, 3, 1)$table)
```

## Interpretation and limits

*TODO (Monika): 3-5 sentences, written after reading the results above.*

- All nine items were asked with identical wording and response scale in waves 1-5, so mean-level and rank-order comparisons across waves are supported.
- No items are reverse-worded; the direction check found only positive inter-item correlations in every wave.
